message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and efficiency. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, general use).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to check compatibility and prices. | | 2 | **Gather Components** | • CPU (Intel/AMD)
• Motherboard (socket, chipset, form factor)
• RAM (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity)
• GPU (if not integrated)
• Storage (SSD/HDD, NVMe or SATA)
• Power Supply Unit (PSU, wattage, 80+ rating)
• Case (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX)
• CPU cooler (stock or aftermarket)
• Operating System (Windows, Linux)
• Peripherals (monitor, keyboard, mouse) | Check compatibility lists on the component sites. | | 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | • Clean, flat, static‑free surface.
• Anti‑static wrist strap or mat.
• Screwdrivers (Phillips #0, #1). | Avoid carpeted floors; static can damage components. | | 4 | **Install the CPU** | • Open the motherboard’s CPU socket latch.
• Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket.
• Gently place it, close latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide. | | 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount on CPU.
• Mount cooler according to its instructions.
• Connect fan header to motherboard. | Use a small amount; too much can spill onto the motherboard. | | 6 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align RAM sticks with slot notch.
• Push firmly until clips click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. | | 7 | **Mount the Motherboard in the Case** | • Align standoffs in the case with motherboard holes.
• Screw motherboard to standoffs. | Use the correct screw length; avoid overtightening. | | 8 | **Install Storage** | • Mount SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot.
• Secure with screws or latch.
• Connect SATA data & power cables if using SATA drives. | For NVMe, insert into M.2 slot and screw down. | | 9 | **Install the Power Supply** | • Place PSU in its compartment (usually bottom rear).
• Secure with screws.
• Route cables neatly. | Make sure the PSU fan faces the intake or exhaust as per case design. | | 10 | **Install the GPU** | • Remove the appropriate expansion slot cover(s) on the case.
• Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws.
• Connect 6‑pin/8‑pin PCI‑e power connectors from PSU. | Ensure the GPU is fully seated; it should click into place. | | 11 | **Connect Case Front Panel** | • Connect power button, reset button, USB, audio, and LED headers to motherboard.
• Refer to motherboard manual for exact pin layout. | Double‑check orientation; reversing can damage headers. | | 12 | **Cable Management** | • Tidy up cables using Velcro ties or zip ties.
• Route cables through cable‑management holes. | Good airflow and easier future upgrades. | | 13 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | • Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
• Power on.
• Enter BIOS (usually Delete/F2).
• Check that CPU, RAM, storage are detected.
• Set boot priority to your OS installation media. | Update BIOS if needed (check motherboard site). | | 14 | **Install Operating System** | • Insert Windows USB/DVD or boot from Linux ISO.
• Follow on‑screen prompts to install OS.
• Install drivers (chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi). | Keep Windows drivers handy; use manufacturer’s website. | | 15 | **Post‑Build Testing** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, MemTest86, 3DMark).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner).
• Verify stability. | If temperatures are high, re‑apply thermal paste or improve case airflow. | | 16 | **Enjoy & Upgrade** | • Install games/software.
• Keep drivers updated.
• Plan future upgrades (more RAM, better GPU, additional storage). | Keep a record of serial numbers for warranty claims. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU & cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated - [ ] Motherboard mounted - [ ] PSU secured - [ ] GPU inserted & powered - [ ] Storage connected - [ ] Front panel headers wired - [ ] Cables managed - [ ] BIOS detects all components - [ ] OS installed - [ ] Drivers updated - [ ] Stress test passed #### Common Pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **CPU not seated** | Re‑open socket latch, align CPU correctly. | | **RAM not recognized** | Ensure sticks are in correct slots; check for BIOS update. | | **GPU not detected** | Verify PCI‑e slot, power connectors, and BIOS settings. | | **High temperatures** | Reapply thermal paste, improve case airflow, check fan orientation. | | **No boot** | Check boot priority, ensure OS media is bootable, verify cables. | --- ### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Compatibility checker & price comparison. - **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
